source_title: LCBO Wine Find: CINSO Reserva Cinsault 2024
newsletter_intro: I love a wine that gives you something a little different without asking you to overthink it. This LCBO find is a great example of that: a grape you don’t see every day, an easy price point, and a style that feels very drinkable. If you’re curious about trying Cinsault, this is a really nice place to start.

instagram_reel.script:
I spotted a grape on LCBO shelves that I don’t see every day: Cinsault. Say it like “san-so.”

This one is the CINSO Reserva Cinsault 2024 from Chile, and it’s a really nice place to start if you’re curious about trying something outside the usual Cabernet-Merlot lane.

It’s medium-bodied, juicy, and fruit-forward, with red berry notes, a little clove, a little anise, and a lively finish.

What I also like is that it can work slightly chilled, so it’s a nice bridge if you usually reach for white or rosé.

And for under $17 at the LCBO, it’s an easy grab for your next wine run.

linkedin.post:
One of the things I love most about the LCBO is when you can spot a grape that gives drinkers something outside the usual lineup.

CINSO Reserva Cinsault 2024 is a good example. It’s a Chilean Cinsault on shelves here for $16.95, and it offers an easy entry point into a variety that many people know more as a blending grape than a stand-alone wine.

For trade and wine-curious consumers alike, that matters. Accessible bottles like this help widen the conversation around what people can drink, how they can drink it, and what they might discover next.

This one also shows how useful Cinsault can be in the glass: medium-bodied, fruit-forward, and versatile enough to work with food or slightly chilled.

It’s the kind of wine that makes exploration feel low-pressure.
